items.title: fix(blackbox-viewer): name PARALYZE in the flight mode tables
items.summary: A direct consequence of my own earlier merged fix. PR #5511 stopped the log viewer dropping every flight mode above bit 31; once that bit became visible it turned out the name table had no entry for PARALYZE, so on firmware 4.0 through 4.5, where that mode lands exactly on bit 31, the viewer labelled it USER1. Every name after the gap was shifted down one. PARALYZE is a sticky mode, latched until power cycle, so a log did not flicker the wrong name once, it carried it for the whole flight, in the status bar and as an annotation on the chart. Two inserted lines. The work was proving the insert is safe everywhere else: I resolved the table for every release from 3.3 to 2026.6 and diffed it index by index against the firmware enum parsed from rc_modes.h at each tag. Bits 0 to 31 match at all of them afterwards, and the pre-3.3 table is deliberately untouched because that firmware has no such mode. Merged two hours after opening.

items.title: fix(blackbox): honour blackbox_disable_servos
items.summary: A setting in the flight controller firmware that silently did nothing. The blackbox logger decides which fields to record by testing a bitmask the pilot configures, and the servo case read `hasServos() && (FIELD_SELECT(SERVO))`. That second operand is an enum constant, 15, not a check, so the expression was always true and the mask was never consulted. Of the twenty selector checks in that function, nineteen wrap it in isFieldEnabled() and this one did not. So blackbox_disable_servos, and the matching Servo checkbox in the Configurator, have never worked: eight servo fields stayed in the log header and in every frame on the aircraft where log bandwidth actually matters, fixed wings and tricopters. One line. Proved it by compiling against the firmware's own header with a static assertion that the operand is non-zero, and confirmed the header and the frame writers read one cached bit so the fix cannot desync a log from its own declaration. It was introduced in 2024 by the same commit that added the setting.

items.title: fix(gps): correct GPS_UBX_CFG_INTF bitmask max to 63
items.summary: PX4 is the drone autopilot that Betaflight's world sits next to, 12.6k stars. A u-blox GPS parameter declares six configuration bits, so its valid range is 0 to 63, but it advertised a maximum of 32. That is the value of the top bit on its own, not all bits set, so every setting from 33 upward was published to ground stations as out of range. One line. The work was in bounding the claim honestly: PX4 never compiles parameter minimums and maximums into the firmware at all, so runtime behaviour cannot change, and in QGroundControl the checkbox path does no validation while only manual numeric entry refuses the value. An earlier draft of mine claimed it blocked a valid configuration; verification showed that was wrong and the PR says what is actually true. The evidence is a before-and-after of the generated metadata through PX4's own generator: two 40,032-line files differing on exactly one line. The project had already made this identical correction on the two sibling parameters in the same file when their sixth bit was added, which is why the fix is uncontroversial.

items.title: fix(qwen36): a truncated multibyte tail made the tokenizer read past the prompt
items.summary: colibri is an inference engine for large mixture-of-experts models written in plain C, 33.5k stars in its first three months. Its server reads exactly the advertised number of bytes from a network prompt into a buffer of that size and hands them straight to the tokenizer, with nothing in between checking the bytes are well-formed UTF-8. If the prompt ended mid-character, a clipped emoji or a cut-off Arabic letter, the decoder reported the character's full length even though the remaining bytes were not there, so the tokenizer walked past the end of the allocation. Without a sanitizer it does not crash: it silently tokenizes whatever sits next in the heap and feeds the model a prompt containing memory the user never sent. The fix is six lines, a verbatim port of the bounds check the project's own sibling engine already had. That sibling even ships a test gating exactly this case, so the argument was not 'I think you have a bug' but 'your own test fails against your other engine'. Proved it with AddressSanitizer on pristine master (heap-buffer-overflow READ, with line numbers), then showed a 452-line differential harness over twenty text categories producing byte-identical output, so valid input is untouched. Merged in under 48 hours with no changes requested.

items.title: Fix RC Smoothing Mode reading a dead MSP_RX_CONFIG byte
items.summary: These Lua scripts let a pilot tune a quad from the radio transmitter instead of a laptop. The Receiver page read the RC Smoothing on/off setting from byte 25 of MSP_RX_CONFIG, but the firmware has written a hardcoded zero there and discarded it on write since API 1.44; the real flag is byte 32. The ON/OFF labels were inverted on top of that. So on every Betaflight 4.3+ quad since 2021 the radio showed the wrong state, and toggling it and saving was a silent no-op that reverted on the next read. Two lines. Proving it is what took the time: I built the firmware as a host binary with Betaflight SITL and spoke MSP to it directly, which showed byte 25 reading zero in both states while byte 32 tracked the setting, and showed the firmware discarding a write to byte 25 while honouring one to byte 32. Cross-checked the offset and the OFF/ON lookup against five release tags, and confirmed every conditional branch in the message writer emits equal widths so the offset cannot depend on which features a board builds. Then ran the tool on real EdgeTX firmware in the WebAssembly simulator: on master the toggle reads OFF against a flight controller that has it ON, and a save reverts; with the fix both behave. Repo had zero open pull requests.

items.title: Graduate role_skills module from Pyrefly excludes
items.summary: PRAXIST carries 33 legacy files excluded from its Pyrefly type checker as declared type debt, with the instruction that each graduates out of the list as it is touched. praxist/core/role_skills.py, 290 lines, was already clean and could leave with no source change, so the fix is a single deleted line. The work was in proving it: reproducing CI locally needs the product-usage-server extra synced and --python-platform linux, without which the run reports phantom import errors and macOS platform-narrowing noise that have nothing to do with the change. Done properly it is 0 errors before and after, matching CI exactly. Proved the exclusion was load-bearing rather than stale by appending a deliberate type error: main reports it as clean, the patch catches it. Note this repo is Fair Source, source-available but not OSI-approved.

items.title: fix(blackbox): show all flight mode flags when bit 31 is set
items.summary: The blackbox log viewer walked the flight-mode bitfield with a signed right shift. `>>=` coerces to int32, so once bit 31 was set the value went negative, the loop ended after one iteration, and every remaining flag was dropped with no indication. Bit 31 is a real mode: PREARM on 2025.12, CRASHFLIP on 2026.6. Flying 2025.12 with a toggle PREARM switch, the values panel read "ARM" for the whole log, and a frame with only high bits set read "0", indistinguishable from no flags at all. Found by reading the source, not from a bug report. Verified the mask reaches the function positive so the truncation is real, that every name table exceeds 32 entries so widening the scan is safe, and that CSV export and the graph annotations were already correct. One-line fix plus a 7-case test that fails on the unpatched code. Merged to master on 10 September 2026 as c5ab3dba, labelled RN: BUGFIX and shipping in release 2026.12. A maintainer requested one change before approving: new files in this repo must carry the GPL header from DEFAULT_LICENSE.md, a rule documented in AGENTS.md but enforced by no tooling, and contradicted by every other file in test/js/. Added it as a separate commit; both reviewers approved within three minutes of each other and it merged fourteen minutes later.

items.title: fix: failsafePhase name table missing comma and stale count
items.summary: A missing comma made C concatenate two string literals, so the failsafe phase table held five entries instead of six and index 3 decoded as "LANDEDFAILSAFE_RX_LOSS_MONITORING". The count was also stale at 4, so phases above 3 fell through to a raw integer. This is the default output path, so every log with a failsafe has decoded wrongly since Feb 2018. Proved it by compiling the project's own source and printing the array, confirmed the firmware enum is append-only from v2.5.0 so no version gating is needed, and completed the table with GPS_RESCUE and AUTOPILOT. Approved by a core maintainer 24 minutes after opening; CI green on Linux and macOS.

items.title: Flight-mode decode: box IDs shift between firmware versions
items.summary: The decoder mislabels every flight mode, and the obvious fix (swap in a current name table) would have been wrong. Blackbox logs boxId_e enum ordinals, not stable MSP identifiers, and those shift between releases: BOXAIRMODE is bit 28 at 3.3.3, 20 across 4.0 to 4.5, and 24 at 2026.6. So the ticket's own claim that bit 24 is AIRMODE holds only for current firmware; on a 4.x log that bit is BOXCAMERA1. Extracted the enum at each release tag to show the drift, proposed a version-gated fix following the repo's existing precedent, and flagged two further defects in the same code. The reporter agreed and asked me to do the port.

items.title: Dead RCC_AHB macro: corrected the ticket's compile analysis
items.summary: A maintainer asked a month earlier whether an unused macro was worth deleting and got no answer. His ticket said it compiles on two MCU families and fails on three; it compiles on none, because the register it expands to is not defined for any supported chip. Proved that with a control search so the negative result could not be a bad path, which also rules out completing the macro as an alternative. Found duplicate RCC_AHB1 definitions in the G4 and F7 arms the ticket missed, and checked the change merges cleanly against two pending platform PRs. The ticket author reacted to the comment.

items.title: Review: linux-aarch64 toolchain fix (hardware confirmation)
items.summary: Betaflight cannot build on ARM Linux at all: the makefile has no toolchain entry for linux-aarch64 and the parse-time error stops the build before it reaches a target, including SITL which needs no cross toolchain. A three-line fix was approved by two maintainers but had sat eight days because none of them had the hardware. Reproduced the failure inside ubuntu:24.04 on Apple Silicon, applied the patch, confirmed both SITL binaries build, and posted the result.

items.title: Perf triage on eslint-plugin-react-hooks: small-repo numbers + TIMING blind spot
items.summary: Profiled ESLint on a ~20-file Next.js app: eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7.1.1 is 30.7% of lint CPU (0.88s of 2.85s sampled), the largest single consumer, yet ESLint's TIMING=all attributes under 1ms to it, so the cost is invisible to the built-in diagnostic. Posted the numbers, the fixed-cost caveat for small repos, and the NODE_ENV measurement (~3%) as corroborating data on the existing perf issue instead of filing a duplicate.

items.title: Bound agent tool frame args so an LLM tool call can't overflow Int and crash the app
items.summary: Frame-valued agent tool args (startFrame, atFrame, toFrame, durationFrames) were only lower-bounded, so an LLM-generated tool call with a value near Int.max decoded cleanly into Int (it is finite, so it passed the finiteness check) and then trapped the whole app on startFrame + durationFrames — an arithmetic trap the tool executor's do/catch cannot intercept. Added a shared maxToolFrame ceiling plus a requireFrameInBounds helper applied next to the existing guards in add_clips, insert_clips, move_clips, set_clip_properties, add_texts, and apply_layout. Same class as the earlier #201 fix. 23 source lines across 4 files, plus 5 end-to-end regression tests driving each tool at Int.max; full 948-test suite green.

items.title: Agent crash: an out-of-range integer frame arg (near Int.max) traps Int arithmetic and kills the app
items.summary: Reported the crash PR #265 fixes, issue-first per their CONTRIBUTING. Confirmed against main with a test that drives add_clips at Int.max: the process is killed with SIGTRAP the moment the tool runs, because the overflow trap escapes the tool executor's do/catch.

Follows the tldr style guide and passes tldr-lint.

items.title: Open projects with a corrupt media.json instead of failing
items.summary: A project package keeps the timeline (project.json) and media manifest (media.json) in separate files, so a corrupt media.json made readProjectPackage throw and blocked the whole open even though the timeline was intact. Degrade a bad manifest to 'media offline' (like a missing one) and preserve the original file so the next autosave cannot overwrite it. +9 tests; full 835-test suite green; verified live in the running app.

items.title: Corrupt media.json makes the entire project unopenable

items.title: Harden agent/MCP numeric tool args against Int(Double) overflow crashes
items.summary: Untrusted numeric tool args hit Int(Double) with no range check, so an out-of-range value traps on the main thread and crashes the editor (reachable from a normal model tool call or any client on 127.0.0.1:19789). Added shared safeInt / clampInt helpers in ToolExecutor and routed every untrusted Double->Int site through them. +overflow regression test; merged.

items.title: Surface XML/FCPXML write failures instead of silently succeeding
items.summary: The XML exporter swallowed write errors with try?, so a failed FCPXML export still hit 100%, logged 'Export finished', and closed the dialog with no file written. Made XMLExporter.export throwing and had ExportService set the error like the video path. +regression test; full 743-test suite green.

items.title: Fix segment-drop trim: store trimEndFrame as a tail amount, not an out-point
items.summary: Dropping a search 'moment' onto the timeline stored trimEndFrame as an absolute end instead of a tail-trim amount, so a 3000-frame clip could claim 6000 source frames, mis-sampling the waveform/thumbnail and the FCPXML export. One-line fix + a new invariant test; also corrected an existing test that had encoded the bug.
